title: What this course asked of parents
intro: HEDGE™ is an invented course for parents. Its reasons are not: each one was taught by a real ministry, newsletter, book, web page or campaign between 1988 and 2026, and some of them were first taught about gay people. This is what that teaching said and asked, in its own words where it can be quoted, with what is known beside it.

sections.heading: It said nobody knew the cause, then listed causes

items.text: A ministry newsletter admitted it in 2019: “Aside from living in a fallen world, no one is certain what causes gender confusion.” Its next three pages list causes anyway: the family, not fitting in with other children, trauma, mental health, a teenager’s experiments, friends, and social media.
items.source: Reconciliation Ministries of Michigan, “The Building Blocks of Gender Confusion”, newsletter article, © 2019, 4 pp.; read on the page images. p. 1; pp. 2–4.

items.text: It began with the family. In 1988 a telephone counselling manual traced a caller’s “false identity” to hurt, and told callers to forgive “those who have hurt them (usually family members)”.
items.source: Exodus International North America, Exodus Telephone Counseling Manual, © 1988, “Transsexuality” tab. National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428, Box 2, Folder 10. Printed pp. 46–47.

items.text: The same roots, “only deeper”: the 2019 newsletter says the building blocks of being trans “are similar to those of homosexuality, yet they go much deeper”.
items.source: Reconciliation Ministries of Michigan, “The Building Blocks of Gender Confusion”, newsletter article, © 2019, 4 pp.; read on the page images. p. 2.

items.text: Then the friends. The 2019 newsletter: “one person in a social group coming out as transgender prompts many more in that social group to come out as transgender.” Psychological bodies answered in 2021 that “rapid-onset gender dysphoria” “is not a diagnostic classification or subtype”, “nor is it under consideration for inclusion in future editions”.
items.source: Reconciliation Ministries of Michigan, “The Building Blocks of Gender Confusion”, newsletter article, © 2019, 4 pp.; read on the page images. p. 4; CAAPS (Coalition for the Advancement & Application of Psychological Science), Position Statement on Rapid-Onset Gender Dysphoria (ROGD), 26 Jul 2021; signatories include the American Psychological Association; read 15 Nov 2026.

items.text: Then the whole culture. A ministry in 2025: “a culture that has been swept up by gender ideology”. Nothing was dropped: the 1988 manual’s “a false identity” is the 2025 post’s “a new, false gender identity”.
items.source: Love & Truth Network, “18 - Responding to Family Members Who Have Embraced Gender Ideology”, blog post on “The Narrow Way”, dated 31 Oct 2025 (the same text archived 10 Apr 2025); read 15 Nov 2026.

items.text: To look for the wound in themselves: a 2002 parents’ booklet recommended a book in which “Compassion also takes responsibility for one’s parental contributions to the child’s pain”.
items.source: Focus on the Family, When a Loved One Says “I'm Gay” (Love Won Out series), © 2002. NMAH.AC.1428, Box 8, Folder 5. Pp. 42–43.

items.text: To watch for signs: “Are you afraid your child may be struggling with gender identity or otherwise heading in a wrong direction?” In 2003 Exodus told churches to watch for “a young boy … or a young girl in our Sunday School classes that might have some gender identity deficits”.
items.source: Focus on the Family, When a Loved One Says “I'm Gay” (Love Won Out series), © 2002. NMAH.AC.1428, Box 8, Folder 5. P. 43; The Christian Post, 5 Aug 2003, report on the July 2003 Exodus assembly; read 15 Nov 2026.

items.text: To watch the child’s phone: “If your children have unmonitored access to the Internet, you are a negligent parent.” The book’s author has software on his children’s phones: “I know how many times they text.”
items.source: ERLC (the Southern Baptist Convention's Ethics & Religious Liberty Commission), Sexual Brokenness and the Hope of the Gospel, © 2014. Pp. 108, 127.

items.text: To have the child prayed for by strangers, by name: a parents’ prayer list promises that each child added will be “prayed for by all the members at least once a day”.
items.source: Sorrowful Hearts, “Parents” page (first archived Dec 2013; live 2026); read 15 Nov 2026.

items.text: After 18, patience: young adults “will have the liberty to make their own choices”, and “It can take 7-10 years for individuals to work through the implications…”
items.source: Love & Truth Network, “18 - Responding to Family Members Who Have Embraced Gender Ideology”, blog post on “The Narrow Way”, dated 31 Oct 2025 (the same text archived 10 Apr 2025); read 15 Nov 2026. Steps 4 and 6.

items.text: To talk to a chat window first: by 2026 the first contact with a conversion programme could be a chat box that, in the dossier’s words, “remembered what you told it, and held you to it”.
items.source: The dossier card “The chat front doors” (documentary; data/dossier/practices.json chatDoors): a ministry's AI Assistant page (menu item Oct 2025; chat widget from June 2026; page printed 14 Nov 2026); a same-sex-attraction newsletter's chatbot (21 Jan 2026); a paid parents' course's chatbot page (printed 14 Nov 2026).

items.text: It told the threat as history: a 2016 opinion piece was titled “Why We Should Have Seen The Transgender Craze Coming” (“Craze” is its own word), and said it “arrived decades ago as a tiny seed”.
items.source: The Federalist, 28 Nov 2016, “Why We Should Have Seen The Transgender Craze Coming” (opinion); read 15 Nov 2026.

items.text: Parenthood became a political identity. A 2026 report on anti-gender movements: religious and populist movements “have strategically and deliberately elevated parenthood as a political identity and the child as a sacred figure around which coalitions can be built”.
items.source: Transnational Institute, State of Power 2026, chapter 9 (“The Innocent Children”), printed p. 83; read on the page image.

items.text: Its word reached governments. A UN expert wrote in 2021 that “gender ideology” is “a linguistic formula used symbolically to refer in an accusatory manner”, born in opposition to the Cairo (1994) and Beijing (1995) conferences. In 2025 a government put the phrase in the title of an executive order.
items.source: UN Independent Expert on sexual orientation and gender identity, report A/76/152, 15 Jul 2021. Executive Order 14168, “Defending Women From Gender Ideology Extremism and Restoring Biological Truth to the Federal Government”, signed 20 Jan 2025; Federal Register, Vol. 90, No. 19 (30 Jan 2025), pp. 8615–8618. Read on its official page, govinfo.gov (content/pkg/FR-2025-01-30/html/2025-02090.htm), on 16 Nov 2026.

items.text: And into election advertising: a 2026 campaign ad closed with “If you care about your children, …”.
items.source: Associated Press, 28 Oct 2026 (via News4JAX): a report on 2026 campaign advertising about transgender people; read 15 Nov 2026.

items.text: Homosexuality left the American Psychiatric Association's manual in December 1973 and the WHO's classification in 1990.
items.source: “Out of DSM: Depathologizing Homosexuality”, Behavioral Sciences 5(4), 2015; WHO ICD-10 F66 (“Sexual orientation by itself is not to be regarded as a disorder”).

items.text: In 2013 DSM-5 replaced “gender identity disorder” with “gender dysphoria”: “gender non-conformity is not in itself a mental disorder”.
items.source: American Psychiatric Association, “Gender Dysphoria Diagnosis” (Nov 2017); read 15 Nov 2026.

items.text: In June 2013 Exodus International, whose 1988 manual opens the tape, shut down, and its president apologised.
items.source: Religion News Service in The Christian Century, issue of 24 Jul 2013; read 15 Nov 2026.

items.text: ICD-11, in force since 1 January 2022, moved gender incongruence out of the chapter of mental disorders.
items.source: WHO, “Gender incongruence and transgender health in the ICD” (FAQ); WHO news, 11 Feb 2022.

items.text: “Rapid-onset gender dysphoria” “is not a diagnostic classification or subtype” in the DSM or the ICD, “nor is it under consideration for inclusion in future editions”.
items.source: CAAPS (Coalition for the Advancement & Application of Psychological Science), Position Statement on Rapid-Onset Gender Dysphoria (ROGD), 26 Jul 2021; signatories include the American Psychological Association; read 15 Nov 2026.
